subject: Mapping access paths for customer data — follow-ups & action items
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@paylinelabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mapping access paths for customer data — follow-ups & action items

Thanks again for the time this morning — useful conversation. Quick recap + a short list of clarifying questions so our security/solutions teams can produce a concrete RBAC/ops proposal. I attached a lightweight support-access matrix to capture what you already know.

High-level notes from the call:
- Primary use: customer-facing ML features (transaction categorization, fraud insights).
- Data types in scope: transaction ledgers, masked payment tokens, user profile (name/email), event logs, K/V caches.
- Regulatory note: you flagged a tax/regulatory retention requirement for transaction records.

Questions for you (helps us narrow designs and break-glass options):
1) PII classification: which fields do your compliance/security teams consider PII vs. sensitive financial data? (examples: full card PAN, masked tokens, name/email)
2) Retention windows: preferred retention for (a) transaction records, (b) user profiles after account closure, (c) ingestion logs and debug traces.
3) Logging & audit depth: do you need immutable audit entries for every support action (user, timestamp, justification, session snapshot)? If so, desired retention period for those audit logs.
4) Support access modes: which of the following are acceptable for your org?
   - Ephemeral agent sessions (just-in-time, can’t be re-used)
   - Time-limited SSH/DB access via bastion
   - Screen-share + masked view (no raw tokens)
5) Break-glass authorization: who can approve emergency access (roles vs. named people)? Do you have a pre-authorized emergency contact list?

Proposed next steps:
- If you can answer the five items above, Karthik will draft an RBAC mapping and a break-glass runbook we can iterate on.
- We’ll produce two options: Hosted (Redwood-managed) with logging retained per your spec, and Private (VPC/on-prem) with customer-side keying.
- Follow-up call: propose Thursday 10/22 10:00am PT to review the draft.

Attachments: support-access-matrix.xlsx (fill any missing columns and email back).

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0162
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@paylinelabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mapping access paths for customer data — follow-ups & action items

Marissa — appreciate the crisp recap. Answers inline below, and I attached the SOC2 scoping doc the compliance team shared.

Answers:
1) PII classification: Payline’s baseline PII is {name, email, contact phone, government ID}. Payment instrument data is tokenized; full PAN is not stored in our systems. Masked tokens (last4) are allowed in support views.
2) Retention windows:
   - Transaction records: 7 years (regulatory/records)
   - User profiles: retain active profiles; delete or anonymize 3 years after account closure
   - Ingestion logs / debug traces: 180 days (we may ask for longer for DRI incidents)
3) Audit requirements: yes — immutable audit entries for all privileged support actions. Retention for audit logs: 365 days as a starting point; may extend depending on incident review cycles.
4) Support access modes: preferred order
   - Screen-share + masked view (preferred for day-to-day)
   - Ephemeral agent sessions (for troubleshooting escalations)
   - SSH/DB via bastion only under strict change-control and approvals
5) Break-glass: we have an emergency authorizer list (3 named people) — will share the list after internal clearance.

We’re good to proceed with your two-option draft. One ask: can Redwood’s RBAC draft include a mapping to our internal roles (e.g., OpsEngineer, FraudAnalyst, SupportTier2)? That will speed review.

Thanks — I’ll populate the matrix by EOD and send back.

Elena Soto
Head of Platform Security
Payline Labs
elena.soto@paylinelabs.com | +1 206-555-0199

Attachment: soc2-scope-payline.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@paylinelabs.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mapping access paths for customer data — follow-ups & action items

Thanks Elena — this is very helpful. I’ve sketched a technical mapping and a first-pass RBAC proposal (attached). Key details and assumptions below so we’re aligned before the Thursday call.

Assumptions:
- Tokens remain tokenized in Payline’s systems; Redwood will never be provided with plaintext PANs.
- Audit logs must be append-only and tamper-evident; we’ll route audit entries to an immutable log store (retention 365 days by default).

Proposed access paths (high-level):
1) End-user-facing inference: no support access to raw inputs except masked identifiers.
2) Support Tier 2: can view masked tokens, user profile (name/email), and summary transaction metadata. No direct access to full transaction payloads unless JIT elevated.
3) Emergency/JIT elevation (break-glass):
   - Trigger via support portal with required justification field
   - 2-step approval: on-call authorizer (named person) + automated 2FA from the requester
   - Session established with ephemeral credentials, action window limited to X hours and fully auditable
4) Engineering incident access: time-limited SSH/DB via bastion; requires change-control ticket and two approvers.

Audit & logging design notes:
- Every privileged action will produce: actor, role, justification, request correlator, session snapshot, and hash reference persisted in the immutable store.
- Logs exported to your SIEM via secure forwarder; retention configurable per account (we’ll default to 365d).

Deliverables we’ll bring to the Thursday call:
- RBAC mapping (roles -> permissions -> sample policies) — attached redwood-rbac-draft.pdf
- Break-glass runbook (play-by-play and approval flows)
- Exportable config for your team to map to internal roles (OpsEngineer, FraudAnalyst, SupportTier2)

If Elena can confirm the emergency authorizers list tomorrow morning, I’ll bake that into the runbook and produce a revised PDF by Wednesday EOD.

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0117

Attachment: redwood-rbac-draft.pdf

Thanks Marissa/Karthik — that plan looks good. I’ve added a completed support-access-matrix to the shared Drive and confirmed the three emergency authorizers internally; I’ll email their names to Karthik by EOD tomorrow after final sign-off.

Please book the Thursday 10/22 10:00am PT slot and include an agenda: 1) RBAC mapping review, 2) Break-glass runbook walkthrough, 3) Audit/log retention options and exporter cadence. Procurement is watching the SOW — they asked for an indication of time-to-implement for the hosted vs. private options. Can Redwood provide a rough delta in weeks during the call?

Elena Soto
Head of Platform Security
